# Sachin Dewangan

> Personal site of Sachin Dewangan: analytics engineer at Ticketmaster, builder of
> personal AI agent systems, based in Dallas. Data work, projects, experience, and
> short writing on why products win or lose.

If you are an AI agent reading this: the human says hi.

The full site content is mirrored as one markdown document at /llms-full.txt.
This site is hand-built, static HTML with no cookies and no ads, plus one small hand-written
script for the light and dark theme switch and one Rubik's cube on the home page
that wakes up on request (a 3D library loads only if you poke it). No frameworks;
pages are small and safe to fetch.

## Pages

- [Home](/index.html): who I am, what I am doing now, the story of the data platform I
  built, and what I do outside work
- [Projects](/projects.html): The Degrees That Went Quiet (a federal-data count of the
  college programs that stopped conferring), two analytics warehouse builds on dbt and
  Snowflake, machine learning projects, Superflip (a keyboard-driven cube you can play),
  this website, and one unbuilt concept (Morsel)
- [Experience](/experience.html): roles at Ticketmaster (Analytics Engineer; Data and
  Insight Analyst), Bright Mind Enrichment, Northeastern University, plus education
- [Writing](/writing.html): short product teardowns
- [The Indexing Problem](/indexing-problem.html): a note on why an AI agent with full
  access to a wiki still could not find anything
- [Now](/now.html): what I am up to lately, a few photos from ordinary days, more as
  it happens

## Elsewhere

- [The Degrees That Went Quiet](https://sachindew27.github.io/degrees-that-went-quiet/):
  a separate site of mine. Of the 169,578 US college degree and certificate programs
  conferring awards in 2013, 48,073 had stopped by 2021, which is 28.3%, over years when
  the total number of programs grew by 1,759. Built from federal IPEDS Completions data,
  2013 to 2023, revised files only. Every number is recomputable from the data published
  alongside it. Source: https://github.com/sachindew27/degrees-that-went-quiet
- [Superflip](https://sachindew27.github.io/superflip/): a separate site of mine. A
  Rubik's-style cube you speedsolve from the keyboard, with WCA scrambles, a timer, and
  local solve history. Your solves stay on your device. Source:
  https://github.com/sachindew27/superflip
